findings.title: Momentum quadrant names and the window's 'Reading' column are wrong when the horizontal horizon is shorter than the vertical one
findings.where: Overview / Momentum (mmCard) and its window; apps/edge-bff/sector/src/cards/ov.ts quad()/reading() and words.ts W.mm.q, foot, read
findings.steps: Open Overview. In Momentum choose horizontal 1W and vertical 1M (both selects offer any pair). Look at Health (1W +2.3%, 1M -0.4%) and the corner names.
findings.expected: A sector up over the short horizon but down over the longer one is 'turning up'; the names must follow which axis is the longer horizon (or the selects must only allow short on Y).
findings.actual: Names are fixed for X=long, Y=short: top-left is always 'TURNING UP' and bottom-right 'TURNING DOWN'. With X=1W, Y=1M Health sits bottom-right labelled TURNING DOWN though it rose this week after a negative month; top-left 'TURNING UP' holds sectors that are down over 1W and up over 1M (turning down). The footer 'Top left = turning up' and the expanded window's Reading column ('Turning up'/'Down on both') and its example sentence have the same fixed meaning. Same with 1W vs 3M, 1W vs YTD, 1M vs 3M... whenever X is shorter than Y.
